notes:
SUMMARY: Helix is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency operator chat + streaming telemetry summarization. Primary ask: clear latency SLOs across streaming vs non-streaming endpoints and alignment on measurement method (client vs server side). They have strict EU residency requirements for a portion of data and want VPC/private deployment for regulated accounts.

KEY REQUIREMENTS / QUANTIFIED TARGETS:
- Interactive operator chat (streaming): p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 450ms (end-to-end, client-observed).
- Non-streaming batch summarization / rerank: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 800ms (server-side measured; include serialization + network).
- Throughput: peak non-streaming 1,200 req/s, sustained 400 req/s; streaming concurrent sessions ~600 with ~15 tokens/s avg emission.
- Availability: 99.95% SLA target for dedicated pool; credits for p99 breaches.
- Cold-start concerns: want baseline for first-request-after-idle vs warm-cached latency (KV cache warm).

MEASUREMENT ALIGNMENT DISCUSSION (what Helix cares about):
- Client vs server timing: Helix insists on client-side end-to-end timings for operator-facing SLOs (includes TLS handshake, proxy hops). They will accept server-side metrics for internal instrumentation so long as differences are documented and a conversion is agreed (typical delta observed during demo ~60-90ms).
- Streaming specifics: define p95/p99 over 'first-byte' and 'complete-stream' separately. They want first-byte p95 <= 200ms and token-streaming rate guarantees to avoid choppiness.
- Percentile windows: prefer sliding 1h windows for operational alerts and 30d window for SLA credit calculations.
- Tail-latency measurement: require explicit definition of whether p99 is computed across all requests or only non-error successful requests (Helix wants both: an "all-success p99" and an "end-user-impact p99" which excludes internal retries).
- Sampling & aggregation: ask for raw histograms or HDR summary, not just point percentiles; want exportable buckets for audits.

RESERVED GPU / CAPACITY PLANNING NOTES:
- Initial ask: a dedicated 4-GPU pool for evaluation, with option to scale to 8 GPUs for peak regional load (EU + NA).
- Request clear throughput guarantees per GPU profile (expected rps with 1-2k token avg sequence lengths).
- Need warm-up policy for autoscaling to avoid p99 spikes during load shifts.

SLA / CONTRACT DISCUSSIONS:
- Legal wants explicit wording around measurement source (client-observed vs platform-observed) and credit triggers tied to p99 for critical endpoints.
- Request for a playbook: Redwood support runbook for incidents impacting p99 in 15-min windows and an escalation path to on-call infra.

QUOTES / VOICE-OF-CUSTOMER:
- CTO (S. Arora): "We can tolerate occasional tail events but we need deterministic limits for operator chat — 450ms p99 max or we lose adoption."
- Eng lead: "If streaming stalls even briefly operator flow becomes unusable; token emit consistency matters more than raw median latency."

INTERNAL ACTIONS / AE NOTES:
- Demo showed client vs server ~75ms gap on NA region; need EU run to quantify residency impact.
- SE to produce benchmarking matrix mapping model variants -> p50/p95/p99 at different seq lengths (short: 32 tokens, medium: 128, long: 512).
- Draft SLA language sent to legal (drive:/pricing/helix-dedicated-proposal.pdf).

RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- How are streaming p99s computed when a session emits multiple partial responses? (Helix prefers per-session full-stream tail and per-chunk first-byte tail).
- Do SLA credits trigger on per-endpoint p99 breaches or aggregated infra-wide p99? They want per-route capability.

SHORT NEXT STEPS:
- Start 2-week PoC: dedicated 4-GPU pool (NA) with workload replay harness and per-request client timing capture.
- Exchange redline of SLA focusing on p99 measurement source and credit formula.
- Price review & reserved GPU commitment discussion in follow-up call.

STICKY NOTES: "Need explicit mapping from model variant -> expected rps @ p95 to size reserved pool."
